questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon choosing my study abroad, it was crucial for me that I chose a contry where the education and local community were good at english. This was due to the fact that I did not want to be educationally or socially limited by not knowing the local language. Further, I wanted to choose a study destination where I could take upon the last 4 courses I had left of my Bachelors, which was challenging enough in itself. Luckily, VU did offer exactly the Clinical Psychology courses I needed. Further, I naturally wanted to choose a place in which I knew I wanted to explore the cities, nature and environment of the country, since this is an important part of exchange to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My stomach hurts just thinking about if I hadn't gone. Go!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There were advisors standing at both the student accomodation and at uni.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: DUWO (accomodation) councelors gave me my key and pointed me to my dorm. The student office helped me with my student ID, getting access to the student library and finding my books.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms with shared toilets and shared kitchens or dorm rooms with shared kitchens and private toilets.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cooking facilities and equipment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is an amazing social opportunity and you live with people from all over the world. However, you need to have a good social battery and prepare yourself mentally that it will be loads of parties (or party noise, if you don't attend), dinners, common cleaning etc. I LOVED it, but I'm also very used to living in dorms back in CPH and when travelling abroad before, but I do know it was quite draining for some who were more introvert or used to living on their own. But I, as a social person who enjoy being with others and always being on the go, LOVED it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's hard to rate, because my process was complicated. I found the perfect minor of 30 ECTS which fit my last courses at UCPH perfectly. However, two months before going abroad, VU told me that I could not get my minor anyway and should choose other courses. However, there were no other matching courses, i.e. my study abroad would just be straight up cancelled. This was very stressing and upsetting of course, as I had planned everything, found someone to lease my home in CPH, signed off courses in UCPH etc. However, the reason why I don't give them a 1, is that after contacting them over and over again, VU did let me into the minor. This was only because I was so insistent, so had it been a nicer (lol) person than me, they would have just been forced to give up, and that is not okay from VU's side according to me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I reached out to the incoming office and they were always quick at replying, but the whole process was still very stressful and felt unsecure.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 10/10 ended up getting the one's I wanted but only because I was super insistent and the VU made an exception.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out and ask whether the minor or courses you want will be offered to exchange student before you get your hopes up - and make them put it in writing, if they say it will be available to exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is higher than at UCPH, but not unbearable or more time-demanding necessarily, if you just keep up from the beginning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There's more weekly assignments and exams every 7th weeks. This was a bit intense to adjust to in the beginning, but it also means that the curriculum for each exam is way smaller along with lower expactations, which is what I mean by the workload not necessarily being rougher, because you do remember stuff when the periods are so short.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Minor of 5 courses (minor called Psychopathology, Health and Prevention 30 ECTS): 
Psychopathology and Prevention
Assessment and Coaching Skills
Diversity in Clinical Practice
Research Toolkit
Psychopharmacology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All 5, they were amazing. There was a lot of practical knowledge and exercises, so you'd never feel like anything was irrelevant for your education, as I've sometimes suffered a bit with at UCPH. The professors are extremely passionate and interactive with the students about the topics, and the whole study-mentality and passion is just higher at the VU. People really wish to learn.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. Everything was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, food, social stuff, going out etc. was cheaper. Public transport (I biked everywhere but when going on day trips for larger citites, e.g. Rotterdam, Hague, Utrecht, Brussels, Paris) was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sport activities, lots of social events, debate clubs, pub quizzes etc. were available - all with a cost naturally.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Find a nice friend group and with them:
Go on weekend trips by flixbus: paris, brussels, rotterdam, utrech, hague, antwerp
Go biking on the country side
Organize your own food- and pub-crawls
Attend gym classes in the parks (often free trials;))

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel travel travel and explore the NL by bus and train

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It will come naturally, first in introduction week, but also via ESN and via the place you live (especially if you live at Uilenstede)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: More extrovert than danish people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Be open and social from the beginning so that you interact and create some lovely friendgroups
2: Go exploring on the weekends, all of a sudden, its over :(
3: Even though there's not a lot of hours of teaching, try to make your own everyday schedule (e.g. 9-16) at uni - that way, even with all the assignments, you're free on nights and weekends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Uilenstede is a great student accomodation if you want the full social exchange experience

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life and getting a feeling of re-inventing myself in new wonderful surroundings

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
